title: The recent Thomists and Molina diametrically opposed
source_text: CVIII. Porro ex dictis facile colligitur recentiorum Thomistarum doctrinam, quam exponit Didacus Alvarez, e diametro oppositam esse doctrinae quam tradit Molina, circa gratiam illam quae dicitur efficax, & cui tribuitur hominis conversio. Prorsus enim inter se pugnant, sive spectetur modus quo gratia hominem movet ad actus quibus ad Deum convertitur, sive natura ipsa & quidditas gratiae, & qua in re illa ponenda est.
pass_a_gloss: CVIII. Moreover from what has been said it is easily gathered that the doctrine of the recent Thomists, which Didacus Alvarez sets out, is diametrically opposed to the doctrine which Molina teaches, concerning that grace which is called efficacious, & to which the conversion of man is attributed. For they fight altogether among themselves, whether the manner be regarded by which grace moves man to the acts by which he is converted to God, or the very nature & quiddity of grace, & in what thing it is to be placed.
pass_b_english: Thesis CVIII. From all this it is easy to see that the doctrine of the recent Thomists, as Diego Alvarez presents it, stands diametrically opposed to Molina's teaching about the grace called efficacious, the grace to which a person's conversion is ascribed. The two are in complete conflict, whether we look at the way grace moves a person to the acts by which he turns to God, or at the nature and quiddity of grace itself and where it is to be located.
